rationale: Remove Pike County Light & Power as a standalone manager-level PortCo and consolidate it with the existing Corning parent record. Pike's current official site identifies it as a Corning Energy Corporation subsidiary and says Argo acquired the Corning parent on July 6, 2022. The Pennsylvania PUC's 2025 indirect-control proceeding shows Pike and Leatherstocking below Corning Energy, ACP Crotona and Argo-managed entities; it does not show a separate Pike-level Argo investment. Use Corning Energy Corporation as the current canonical parent name, preserve Corning Natural Gas Holding Corporation and Pike identities as aliases and subsidiary history, and retire the existing duplicate Corning production identity into the immutable queue target. The proposed Apollo indirect-control transaction did not close and was terminated in January 2026, so Argo remains current and no pending ownership transaction is recorded.

beforeImage.name: Pike County Light & Power
beforeImage.description: Pike County Light & Power is a regulated electric and natural gas utility serving communities in northeastern Pennsylvania. The utility provides local distribution service to residential, commercial, and other customers through an asset-heavy model based on owned and operated utility infrastructure. Company materials state that it was incorporated on May 17, 1910 and continues to operate from Milford with defined electric and gas service territories in Pike County. The business is a local franchise utility rather than a merchant power or unregulated energy-services platform. Public filings show that the utility sits alongside Leatherstocking Gas in a regional regulated-utility ownership chain associated with Argo Infrastructure Partners, while public sources do not disclose the current operating-company ownership percentages.

afterImage.name: Corning Energy Corporation
afterImage.subsector: Regulated natural gas and electric distribution
afterImage.description: Corning Energy Corporation is the parent platform for regulated natural gas and electric distribution utilities in New York and Pennsylvania, including Corning Natural Gas Corporation, Pike County Light & Power Company and Leatherstocking Gas Company. Pike is an operating subsidiary rather than a separate manager-level infrastructure investment. Corning's operating history dates to 1904, its holding company was formed in 2013, and it acquired all of Pike's stock from Orange & Rockland on August 31, 2016. Argo Infrastructure Partners completed the acquisition of 100% of the Corning parent platform on July 6, 2022 through the ACP Crotona ownership chain. A 2025 application proposed replacing the Argo general partner with an Apollo-controlled general partner, but the transaction did not close and was terminated in January 2026. Argo therefore remains the current owner, and no signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 16, 2026.

milestones.event: Corning Natural Gas, the principal regulated utility operating company and predecessor of the current Corning Energy platform, was incorporated.
Pike County Light & Power Company, now a regulated operating subsidiary of Corning Energy, was incorporated in Pennsylvania.
Corning Natural Gas Holding Corporation was formed as the public parent of Corning Natural Gas and its utility investments; it was later renamed Corning Energy Corporation.
Corning Natural Gas Holding Corporation acquired all outstanding stock of Pike County Light & Power from Orange & Rockland Utilities, adding Pike as a regulated subsidiary.
Argo Infrastructure Partners completed the acquisition of 100% of Corning's common and preferred stock through the ACP Crotona ownership chain.
The Pennsylvania PUC held a hearing on an application for an indirect change of control of Corning Energy and its Pike and Leatherstocking subsidiaries involving Apollo and Argo-affiliated entities.
Argo, ACP Crotona Holdings and Apollo withdrew the New York petition after the proposed general-partner transaction failed to close and was terminated.
